drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 49-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 1.52, creatinine 0.91, hemoglobin 13.6, lactate 1.7-3.1, platelets 127, sodium 139, wbc 19.4; vitals dbp 49-59, heart_rate 105-118, map 61-73, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 22-25, sbp 86-100, spo2 97, temp 38.3-39
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Blood cultures x2; Lactated Ringer's 30 mL/kg IV bolus; Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.87, hemoglobin 13.5, platelets 136, sodium 139, wbc 15; vitals dbp 63-68, heart_rate 86-102, map 79-85, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 17-20, sbp 109-122, spo2 96-98, temp 37.2-38
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 49-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
